item.title: 'Bolsonaro win could put EU-Brazil ties at risk,' says former MEP Albuquerque
item.description: A Bolsonaro victory could push Brazil further from the European Union, according to Portuguese political analyst and former MEP João Albuquerque. He says Lula helped bring the two sides closer on trade, climate and democratic values, including progress on the Mercosur deal.

item.title: FBI arrests woman accused of spying on Taiwanese president's family in the US for China
item.description: Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te condemned the incident and slammed China for its blatant disregard of human rights and suppression of personal freedoms, in what he labelled a “barbaric” act.

item.title: Euro hits 17-month low as French debt fears mount and Spain heads for snap election
item.description: The euro slid to its weakest level against the US dollar since May 2025 on Monday, as France's debt troubles and Spain's political turmoil, capped by a snap election call, fuelled fears of a fresh eurozone crisis and of contagion across the bloc's bond markets.

item.title: Belgian city’s historic canals turn green after record-hot summer
item.description: A thick carpet of green duckweed has covered Ghent’s canals, disrupting tour boats and raising fresh concerns about climate change in Belgium.

item.title: Israel bars UK Green leader after party votes to define Zionism as racism
item.description: UK Jewish groups say the motion stokes hatred after a string of attacks on their community, while the government and other parties have condemned a policy that even at least three out of five Green MPs opposed.

item.title: Iran war: 'Europe not being at the table is a failure', Charles Michel says
item.description: Former European Council President Charles Michel says the EU must have a stronger role in resolving conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

item.title: Nobel Prize 2026 kicks off: Who will win the medicine award?
item.description: The 2026 Nobel Prize season begins with the physiology or medicine award, announced at Stockholm's Karolinska Institute.

item.title: All-inclusive to adventure: The top experiences that will shape ultra-luxury travel in 2027
item.description: Planning next year’s ultra-luxury escape? All-inclusives, celebrations and privacy are among the experiences driving high-end traveller habits.

item.title: What’s next for EU migration policy? Take our poll
item.description: EU ministers are moving to tighten migration policy, with new return rules, stronger Frontex powers, expanded border surveillance and deeper cooperation with countries of origin and transit. Is the EU handling migration effectively?

item.title: Dogs, turtle and snail receive blessings in churches
item.description: Pets from dogs to turtles received holy water blessings in Manila and Santiago as Catholics marked Saint Francis of Assisi, patron saint of animals.

item.title: Spain's Sánchez calls snap election for 29 November after housing defeat
item.description: Sánchez spent the weekend in consultations, seeking to capitalise politically on Spain's growing housing crisis, while a migration crisis in Ceuta and corruption cases involving figures close to his Socialist Party piled pressure on his government.

item.title: Glastonbury 2027 tickets sell out in 42 minutes – with line-up still unannounced
item.description: Organisers announced last month that general admission tickets would cost £408 each, including a £5 booking fee – taking the price above £400 for the first time.

item.title: Floods leave streets and roads submerged across Catalonia
item.description: Two people have died and another is missing after heavy rain caused flooding across Catalonia, with firefighters responding to more than 1,500 calls.

item.title: How is Europe tightening borders and speeding up returns? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
item.description: The EU is toughening its migration policy, just months after rolling out the Migration and Asylum Pact. But where does it want to invest, and what tools does it plan to use? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

item.title: Spanish police remove over 3,000 migrants from Ceuta beach camp
item.description: Police dismantle a migrant camp on Ceuta’s Trampolín Beach, moving over 3,000 people from tents to a temporary reception centre for processing.

item.title: Merz and Mathernová send a message to Moscow from Kyiv
item.description: Good morning, Brussels. It’s Monday, and I am Angela Skujins. On today’s agenda: Friedrich Merz in Kyiv, Charles Michel on "our commo future", and the Brazilian ballot. Let’s dive in.

item.title: Five days of intense rainfall leave trail of destruction across Crete
item.description: An 80-year-old farmer has been found dead and eight national park workers are stranded in the Samaria Gorge, as ministers head to the island and EU satellites map the affected areas.

item.title: Why ordinary investors struggle to buy into the robotics boom
item.description: Most of the companies building the robots of the future are still private, leaving ordinary investors with limited options such as Tesla, diversified industrial groups or new vehicles like RoboStrategy, a Nasdaq-listed fund whose shares trade at more than twice the value of its assets.

item.title: Social reckonings and 90s nostalgia: The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week
item.description: Jeremy Strong plays Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg in 'The Social Reckoning', Stephen King's 'Carrie' is adapted for the small screen, and Tate Britain revives the rebellious creativity of the 90s. Here's what to look out for this week.

item.title: Europe Today: Russia hits Kyiv as Merz visits; Bolsonaro wins Brazil's first round election
item.description: German Chancellor Friedriz Merz's visit to Ukraine was met with Russian missiles as he pledged €1.3 billion to Kyiv. In Iran, the country's deputy foreign minister says Washington is reviewing Tehran’s proposal to end the war. And in Brazil, Bolsonaro wins Brazil's first round election.

item.title: US pulls all B-1 bombers from UK airbase at centre of terror probe
item.description: Donald Trump has criticised the UK authorities decision to release six men on bail after they were arrested following an incident near airbase RAF Fairford.

item.title: Serb separatist politician Milorad Dodik thanks Trump, Putin as he declares victory in contested Bosnia vote
item.description: Pro-Russia Serb nationalist politician Milorad Dodik – who is serving a six-year ban from holding public office for defying rulings of Bosnia’s international envoy and Constitutional Court, claimed victory on Sunday, saying his party would hold a “vast majority”.

item.title: Tooth with jade inlay reveals ancient Maya skill as dentists
item.description: A study of a pre-Hispanic molar with a jadeite inlay concludes it was treated while its owner was still alive. The find is the first documented case of such an inlay in a Mayan back molar.

item.title: Coral reefs are bleaching in extreme heat. Could underwater umbrellas save them?
item.description: Underwater shades could help corals survive extreme heat, but researchers stress that they’re not a catch-all solution.

item.title: The best road trips to spot Europe’s most impressive wildlife
item.description: Planning a wildlife escape? These European road trips combine spectacular scenery with some of the continent’s best opportunities for spotting animals in the wild.

item.title: Intelligence Everywhere: Inside Europe’s Next Technology Era
item.description: AI is moving beyond the screen. Featuring Qualcomm engineers and leaders, this documentary explores how hybrid AI, edge computing, open innovation and 6G could transform smartphones, smart glasses, cars and robots, and what role Europe will play in the next era of AI.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 5th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 5th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: This industry adds €65 billion to the European economy, but is its bad reputation fair?
item.description: The cruise industry is attracting younger travellers, but how is it addressing concerns over emissions and overtourism?

item.title: Brazil heads to a runoff presidential vote after Bolsonaro and Lula fail to acquire outright majority needed
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, Brazilian senator, presidential hopeful and son to embattled former leader Jair, says he is “very happy” to have led in the first round and heading into the runoff, with incumbent Lula expressing disappointment over “unexpected” results.

item.title: Judo 2026 World Championships: Koga and Yusifov Strike Gold on Opening Day in Baku
item.description: Wakana Koga claimed her first world title at -48kg, defeating Assunta Scutto in the final. At -60kg, home favourite Ahmad Yusifov came from behind to beat Sherzod Davlatov, sending the Baku crowd into celebration on an unforgettable opening day.

item.title: Sánchez in talks with coalition partners on reflection day: will he call elections in Spain?
item.description: The Spanish prime minister is weighing an early election after parliament rejected his housing plans, amid protests over the weekend. 29 November is the earliest possible date.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 4th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 4th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: “We don't feel a sense of worry” in Europe, says the head of the Muslim World League
item.description: While in Brussels to meet with political and religious leaders, Sheikh Dr Mohammad bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa stressed the need to deepen dialogue in order to confront the turmoil facing the world and that Europe's "civilised constitutions" will prevent political excesses.

item.title: Student protests in France: 400–500 schools fully or partially closed Monday
item.description: Another day of mobilisation is planned for Tuesday. By then, 400 to 500 secondary schools are expected to remain fully or partially closed, including 24 that have been “burned or vandalised”. The ministry also reports that 78 education staff have been injured since the movement began.

item.title: Has plague returned to Siberia? Panic in Russia after death of lab worker
item.description: A female staff member at an anti-plague institute in the Irkutsk region who died amid rumours of a "black death" outbreak was diagnosed with "pneumonia of unknown origin". Rospotrebnadzor insists that the situation in the region is "stable".

item.title: Brazilians vote in first round of presidential election
item.description: Nearly 160 million Brazilians were eligible to vote in Sunday's presidential election. Polls close at 17:00 Brasília time. With voting conducted digitally, the first results are expected about three hours later, overnight in Europe

item.title: Two people have died in Catalonia as the region is hit by torrential rain and flooding
item.description: On Sunday, Spanish Civil Protection sent a new Es-Alert to five Catalan counties reminding residents of travel restrictions, after Barcelona saw its wettest day in at least 20 years and the Besòs river passed the danger threshold.

item.title: 'I have complete confidence in Jordan': Le Pen backs Bardella after three days of silence
item.description: After three days of silence, the National Rally's French presidential candidate has responded to Mediapart's release of new alleged evidence of antisemitic remarks by the party leader.

item.title: Merz makes surprise visit to Kyiv: Germany pledges further aid to Ukraine
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv on Sunday. Accompanied by Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and representatives of German defence and energy companies, he aims to pledge further military and financial support for Ukraine.

item.title: Latvia's pro-European ruling party wins election as populists gain ground
item.description: With more than 99.9 per cent of votes counted, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' United List party was in the lead with 35.4 percent, according to state TV.

item.title: Off the Record: Teflon Rutte is on a mission to keep NATO together
item.description: Every week, Euronews' Chief Europe Editor Maria Tadeo breaks down the stories that made the week in Brussels and beyond. This week: her exclusive interview with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte — a man with Teflon skin.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 4th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 4th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Spanish police clear Ceuta's largest migrant camp ahead of King and Queen's visit
item.description: Police undertook Operation Trampolín on Sunday to clear a makeshift settlement on Ceuta's Trampolín beach, home to about 3,000 people living in poor conditions for more than two months.

item.title: FlyDubai captain said “I had one more fight left in me” and opened cockpit door
item.description: FlyDubai hero captain Smit Machchhar described to Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu how the attack started and how he managed to finally open the cockpit door after nearly losing his vision under the co-pilot’s repeated blows. “I knew I couldn't let the passengers die,” Machchhar said.

item.title: 'I want to spark new ideas': Architect Ma Yansong on designing the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
item.description: Last month, film producer George Lucas opened his long-awaited Museum of Narrative Art for many legions of fans of Star Wars memorabilia and visual storytelling. Ma Yansong, the Chinese architect who designed the futuristic looking building, says he hopes it "sparks curiosity and new ideas."

item.title: North Korea fires intermediate-range missile, claiming evasive flight and AI features
item.description: Japan’s military said the missile landed in waters outside its exclusive economic zone, while South Korea's military, which often accuses the North of exaggerating its capabilities, said it travelled more than 700 kilometres.

item.title: Bosnia awaits for final general election results as preliminary count remains unclear
item.description: Around 3.4 million eligible voters in Bosnia headed to the polls to choose the three members of the country’s multi-ethnic presidency, lawmakers for the national Parliament, and heads of institutions for the country’s two entities.

item.title: Increasing influence: Italy marks 800 years since death of Saint Francis of Assisi
item.description: Ceremonies and events are being held in Assisi throughout the day in honour of Italy's patron saint. The festivities form part of the Franciscan Jubilee Year, proclaimed by Pope Leo XIV.

item.title: The eyes have it: Iconic World Cup pictures explored by Getty photographers
item.description: Whether on or off the pitch, many of the most memorable moments from FIFA World Cups have been captured by Getty. Here, some of the photographers behind those lenses share their thoughts about taking the best emotive images.

item.title: Shooting and scoring: Photographer Alex Pantling on capturing the world’s greatest footballers
item.description: Getty photographer Alex Pantling reported on the FIFA World Cup 2026 and shared with European Lens his reflection on the experience along with some of his favourite shots from the tournament.
